critical_code_review_comments: ROOT CAUSE of the iter_18 'HTTP 403' bug AND the post-fix 'body stream already read' bug: in this preview environment (React 19 + StrictMode + Cloudflare ingress + dev tooling) the Response body of error responses is being drained between fetch resolution and our await res.text(). Even res.clone().text() returns empty string. Backend curl confirms {"detail":"PIN salah"} is wire-delivered correctly (content-length: 22). Verified by inspecting the bundled JS — the source-correct fix is in place but body-read fails. The pragmatic fix shipped here is a status-based fallback (403 → 'PIN salah', 422 → 'Masukkan PIN 4 digit') that runs only when bodyText is empty/non-JSON. This is robust because /api/auth/staff-pin has only one error semantic per status. Note: this same body-stream draining anomaly likely affects other error paths in the codebase (PipelineDashboard/AdminDashboard/AttendanceKiosk all do `await res.json()` after !res.ok) — main agent should consider applying the same defensive pattern (clone+text+JSON.parse with status-based fallback) where user-facing error toasts matter.

OwnerProtectedRoute behavior verified end-to-end: hacker session cookie → /me returns 403 → AuthContext.checkAuth catches and sets user=null → /admin renders [data-testid=owner-login-page]. Defense-in-depth at /me is working as designed.
Auth.py /me whitelist re-check is correctly invariant on email casing (uses .lower().strip()) and matches the same normalization applied in /session exchange — no bypass via mixed-case email.

rca of the issue: iter_18 'HTTP 403' + iter_19 'body stream already read' BOTH had the SAME root cause: in this Cloudflare-fronted React-19+StrictMode dev environment the Response body of !res.ok responses is consumed (or never delivered to JS) before our await res.text() executes. Even res.clone().text() returns empty string — meaning the original body never made it into the JS Response object's stream. Backend curl confirms `{"detail":"PIN salah"}` is wire-delivered with content-length 22. Cannot diagnose further without browser-level instrumentation; could be the Cloudflare error-page interception, a service worker, devtools instrumentation, or React 19's experimental fetch caching. Mitigation shipped: client-side status-based fallback message map covering the only two error statuses /staff-pin returns (403 + 422). Safe because the endpoint has fixed error semantics. To reproduce iter_18 bug: revert to `await res.json()` after `if (!res.ok)` — fails with 'body stream already read' in this env. To reproduce the wire-correct body: `curl -X POST $URL/api/auth/staff-pin -d '{"pin_code":"9999"}' -H 'Content-Type: application/json'` shows body intact.
